articles.title: Why Do Some People Say 'Warsh' Instead of 'Wash'?
articles.summary: Have you ever heard someone say "warsh" instead of "wash"? It's not a mistake—it's part of an old American dialect. Linguists trace it back to Scotch-Irish immigrants who brought strong "r" sounds. Today, you might still hear it from older folks in places like Appalachia.

articles.title: Trump Says Iran Peace Deal Might Happen—Then Threatens More Bombs
articles.summary: President Trump paused a mission to guide ships near Iran, saying a peace deal was close. But the next day, he warned that if no deal happens, bombing could get even worse. Experts say talks are tricky, and Iran says the U.S. must give more.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV Will Open a Giant Tower and Meet Migrants in Spain
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV is visiting Spain in June! He'll inaugurate a huge tower at Barcelona's famous Sagrada Familia church—it's now 172.5 meters tall. He'll also meet migrants in the Canary Islands, where thousands arrive from Africa. It's a trip full of big moments.
